_comment: Pinned static ffmpeg/ffprobe builds for the desktop sidecar (ADR-0019 §3).
Empty on purpose: choosing where these binaries come from is a supply-chain
and licensing decision for the project owner, not something to inherit from
whatever a build script happened to hardcode. Any practical static ffmpeg
includes libx264 and is therefore GPL, so publishing it carries source-offer
A package-manager ffmpeg will NOT work: Homebrew's is a thin binary over a
large dylib closure under its own prefix, so a copy runs on the build
machine and nowhere else. The build must be genuinely static.
To populate: pick a source, download it, record the URL and sha256 here,
then run `python packaging/fetch_ffmpeg.py`. build_sidecar.py refuses to
bundle a binary whose checksum does not match this file.
Until this is populated, build with --skip-ffmpeg; the sidecar then falls
back to a system ffmpeg via media/tool_paths.py, which works on a developer
machine but not on a user's.
